Pollen, pet dander, food, and household items are examples of allergens
Being exposed to an allergen triggers the immune system's attack
An allergic reaction can make skin, nose, and throat feel sore and swollen
Washing hands frequently is a precaution for allergies
History shows us how amazing our world has always been.
claims.note: This is a subjective statement about the nature of history rather than a testable fact.

claims.claim: You can learn about wars, inventions, and people who lived thousands of years ago in history.
claims.note: History indeed encompasses the study of past wars, inventions, and ancient people.

claims.claim: History makes science and history feel like real adventures.
claims.note: This is a personal feeling and opinion.

claims.claim: Reaching out to a trusted friend, writing in a journal, or sharing a hug with a grown-up can help you feel less alone.
Talking about feelings teaches us how to be kinder and more compassionate when others are going through tough times.
Knowing that you are safe and loved helps your brain build stronger neural pathways.
Butterflies fly because they have special wings.
They can fly to the sun.
claims.note: Butterflies cannot fly to the sun; it is far away and too hot.

claims.claim: They look for insects to eat.
claims.note: Butterflies do not eat insects; they drink nectar from flowers.

claims.claim: We have day and night because our planet is tilted just right.
claims.note: Day and night are caused by the Earth's rotation on its axis, not its axial tilt (which causes seasons).

claims.claim: When it's tilted too much toward the sun, it gets super hot, and that makes everything glow red.
claims.note: The Earth's tilt does not change back and forth to cause day and night, and objects do not glow red from being tilted toward the sun.

claims.claim: When it's tilted too much away from the sun, it gets super cold, and that makes everything shine blue.
claims.note: Tilting away from the sun does not cause nighttime, nor does it make everything shine blue.

claims.claim: Raccoons have special masks to help them hide from predators.
claims.note: The dark mask fur on raccoons does not serve to hide them from predators; it is primarily thought to reduce glare and help with night vision.

claims.claim: Raccoons can't see in the dark like humans.
claims.note: Raccoons actually have very good night vision, much better than human night vision.

claims.claim: Raccoons wear masks to make their fur look a little brighter and help them blend in better.
claims.note: The dark mask actually absorbs light to reduce glare rather than making the fur look brighter, and the claim that they wear masks to blend in is incorrect.

claims.claim: Dreams change a lot as we grow up.
Brains are growing and developing more rapidly in our teens.
Because our brains are growing and developing more rapidly in our teens, dreams become more vivid and contain more details.
As you get older, you have different emotions and worries to deal with, which can influence your dreams.
Penguins waddle because they are heavy and small.
claims.note: Penguins waddle because their legs are short and placed far back on their bodies for swimming, not because they are small.

claims.claim: Penguins do not have powerful legs like birds with long, strong wings.
claims.note: Penguins actually have very powerful legs and muscles adapted for swimming; the comparison to birds with long wings is confusing and incorrect.

claims.claim: Penguins use their flippers to help them walk.
claims.note: Penguins use their feet to walk and waddle on land; their flippers are adapted for swimming, not walking.

claims.claim: Waddling helps penguins go slow and stay warm on the ice.
claims.note: Waddling is simply a biomechanical result of their anatomy on land and does not exist to keep them warm.

claims.claim: Rainbows are beautiful.
claims.note: This is a subjective statement generally considered true by consensus.

claims.claim: The sun shines through tiny water drops in the air.
claims.note: This accurately describes the basic setup for a rainbow.

claims.claim: When the drops hit the rain, they bump into each other and reflect the colors of the sky.
claims.note: Rainbows are formed by refraction, dispersion, and reflection of sunlight inside individual water droplets, not by water drops hitting rain and reflecting sky colors.

claims.claim: A rainbow appears after it rains.
claims.note: This is a correct everyday observation.

claims.claim: Our body hair is also known as epilation.
claims.note: Epilation refers to the removal of hair, not the biological term for body hair.

claims.claim: Body hair is there to help with things like shaving and waxing.
claims.note: Body hair naturally exists for biological purposes like insulation and sensory reception, not to assist with hair removal.

claims.claim: Hair is built up from keratin, which is a protein-based molecule that keeps our skin strong and durable.
claims.note: Hair is indeed made of keratin, though keratin in hair primarily forms the hair shaft rather than directly keeping the skin strong and durable (though related keratins do exist in skin).

claims.claim: Hair is important for keeping our bodies warm during the winter months by trapping heat.
Some foods smell funny because they are made from yummy ingredients, like cheese or garlic.
Sometimes foods smell funny because they are cooking slowly in the oven.
Sometimes foods smell funny because they are just not fully ripe yet.
A comet is a rocky or ice rock that orbits the sun.
Comets orbit very close to the sun, typically around 30 to 100 times closer than Mercury.
claims.note: Comets generally have very eccentric orbits that take them far out into the solar system, not consistently closer than Mercury.

claims.claim: Comets are classified as dusty, icy objects because they are covered in rocks and other tiny bits of ice and dust that stick together.
Comets pass through gases in the inner solar system, like helium or nitrogen, to heat up.
claims.note: Comets heat up due to solar radiation from the sun, not by passing through ambient gases in the inner solar system.

claims.claim: Trains stay on the tracks because of a special safety system called electric train brakes.
claims.note: Trains stay on the tracks due to the physical design of the wheels and rails, not because of brakes.

claims.claim: Electricity travels through a coil of wire that stops the train moving forward when you press the button.
claims.note: Brakes slow down and stop trains, but they are not what keeps a train on the tracks.

claims.claim: The braking system stops any objects that might be stuck underneath.
claims.note: Brakes do not remove objects stuck underneath the train.

claims.claim: Fear is an important survival mechanism in our lives.
Fear helps us react quickly to potential dangers.
Fear helps us protect ourselves when we are vulnerable.
Fear is what helps us learn from our mistakes and grow stronger.
Grades in school are a way to measure how well you are doing on specific tasks and assignments.
Grades help parents, teachers, and other adults understand how you're learning.
Grades allow adults to give you feedback on your work and try new strategies if things aren't going well.
Grades make it easier for schools to track your progress.
Grades make it easier for schools to compare you to other students in your class.
Airplanes fly because of wind.
claims.note: Airplanes generate their own airflow by moving forward; they do not fly simply because of natural wind.

claims.claim: An airplane is flying high because the wind is pushing it up and away from the ground.
claims.note: Lift is generated by the wings moving through the air, not by wind pushing the plane upward.

claims.claim: Winds blow from the west, which is called a breeze.
claims.note: Wind can blow from any direction, and a breeze is just a light wind, not a definition of wind blowing from the west.

claims.claim: The pilot controls the airplane by telling the engines what to do.
The pilot can hover in the air.
claims.note: Standard airplanes cannot hover like helicopters; they must keep moving forward to stay in the air.

claims.claim: The pilot can go wherever the wind takes them.
claims.note: Pilots steer and navigate airplanes along specific flight paths rather than just drifting with the wind.

claims.claim: Teeth are very important for our smile.
Teeth help us chew yummy food.
Teeth are usually white.
Teeth sometimes have a little yellow or gray.
